title: Bulking Diet NZ
meta_desc: Learn how to gain muscle without fat with a clean bulk diet. Discover NZ high-calorie healthy foods, calorie surplus targets, and timing protein around workouts.
intro: For New Zealand gym-goers, a bulking diet can be an effective way to build muscle. However, it's essential to focus on a clean bulk rather than a dirty bulk to avoid excess fat gain. In this guide, we'll explore the principles of a clean bulk diet and provide practical tips for NZ gym-goers. With the right nutrition programme, you can achieve your fitness goals and maintain a healthy lifestyle.

sections.heading: Clean Bulk vs Dirty Bulk
sections.body: A clean bulk diet involves consuming a calorie surplus of nutrient-dense foods to support muscle growth. In contrast, a dirty bulk diet relies on high-calorie, high-fat, and high-sugar foods, which can lead to excessive fat gain. For a clean bulk, aim for a daily calorie surplus of 250-500 calories above your maintenance level. This can be achieved by increasing your daily food intake or adding supplements like protein powder. NZ brands like Balance and Horleys offer affordable protein powder options, with prices starting from $30 per kilogram.
list: Focus on whole foods like lean meats, fish, eggs, dairy, and whole grains
Include healthy fats like nuts, seeds, and avocados

sections.heading: NZ High-Calorie Healthy Foods
sections.body: New Zealand supermarkets offer a range of high-calorie healthy foods that can support a clean bulk diet. Some examples include full-fat dairy products from brands like Fonterra and Westland, nuts and seeds from retailers like Countdown and New World, and lean meats like chicken and beef from local butchers. When shopping at NZ supermarkets, look for affordable options like canned tuna and salmon, which can provide a convenient source of protein and healthy fats.

sections.heading: Timing Protein Around Workouts
sections.body: Protein is essential for muscle growth and repair. To maximise the benefits of protein, it's crucial to time your intake around workouts. Aim to consume 20-30 grams of protein within 30-60 minutes after exercise, when your muscles are most receptive to nutrient uptake. You can achieve this by drinking a protein shake or eating a meal that includes a source of protein like chicken, fish, or eggs. Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme can also help you access affordable fitness programmes and nutrition advice.
list: Consume protein within 30-60 minutes after exercise
Aim for 20-30 grams of protein per serving
Choose a protein source that suits your dietary needs and preferences

sections.heading: Realistic Expectations
sections.body: A clean bulk diet requires patience and dedication. It's essential to set realistic expectations and focus on progressive overload, which involves gradually increasing the weight or resistance you lift over time. Aim to gain 0.5-1 kilogram per week, and be prepared to make adjustments to your diet and training programme as needed. With the right mindset and nutrition programme, you can achieve your fitness goals and maintain a healthy lifestyle.
